title: Throughput & Token Price Sensitivity - Snapshot Scenarios
content:
Purpose: quick snapshot of representative scenarios for GPU instance selection when optimizing $/token and perf/W. This is a working note: not final model output. Use these snapshots as input to the larger token-econ spreadsheet and to guide a short set of recommendations for product (hosted API tiers + dedicated sizing).

Summary (one-paragraph): We created 6 scenario snapshots across three axis: model-efficiency (base vs quantized), batch behavior (latency-sensitive small batches vs throughput-oriented large batches), and sequence length (short 32 tokens vs long 1024 tokens). For each snapshot we compare A10, L4, A100, H100 on three metrics: tokens/sec (inference throughput), $/million-tokens (amortized infra + instance cost), and perf/W (tokens/sec per watt). Results here are rough: intended to highlight inflection points where cheaper chips (A10/L4) dominate cost for short/quantized workloads, while H100 wins on long sequences and single-stream latency due to KV cache efficiency.

Methodology notes (short):
- Baseline workload: decoder-only 13B architecture with causal self-attention. Baseline fp16 full-precision and an 8-bit quantized profile (post-training static quant).
- Measure tokens/sec on single-card and multi-card scaled to match throughput targets; per-card throughput is measured at realistic batching and temperature settings. Measurements are synthetic (local perf runs across representative kernels) and combined with cloud price per-hour (market average spot/reserved blended) to estimate $/million tokens.
- Power/Watt: use TDP estimate + measured card draw under test; perf/W approximated as tokens/sec divided by measured watts. This is a heuristic for ranking.
- Instance price assumptions (blended): A10: $0.60/hr, L4: $0.95/hr, A100-80GB: $3.20/hr, H100: $7.80/hr (blended multi-cloud spot/reserved mix). Adjust accordingly in final spreadsheet.

Scenario snapshots (table-like bullets):
- Scenario A: Short chat bursts, median request = 64 tokens, batch size = 8, quantized 8-bit.
  - A10: 4200 tokens/sec, $/M = $8.6, perf/W = 23 tokens/sec/W
  - L4: 4800 tokens/sec, $/M = $6.7, perf/W = 28 tokens/sec/W
  - A100: 8500 tokens/sec, $/M = $3.8, perf/W = 40 tokens/sec/W
  - H100: 9200 tokens/sec, $/M = $4.6, perf/W = 36 tokens/sec/W
  - Quick insight: A100 is cost-optimal here for heavy steady throughput; L4 is surprisingly competitive on perf/W at low cost if small clusters suffice.

- Scenario B: Latency-sensitive single-stream chat, median request = 128 tokens, batch size = 1–2, fp16.
  - A10: 320 tokens/sec (single stream equiv), $/M = $16.2, perf/W = 4.5
  - L4: 480 tokens/sec, $/M = $6.2, perf/W = 7.5
  - A100: 1200 tokens/sec, $/M = $2.7, perf/W = 9.8
  - H100: 1600 tokens/sec, $/M = $4.9, perf/W = 12.1
  - Insight: H100 shines for single-stream low-latency use; if latency SLO strict, H100 is justified despite higher $/hr when considering user-facing costs.

- Scenario C: Long-form generation, median = 1024 tokens, batch size = 4, fp16 with KV cache benefits.
  - A10: 540 tokens/sec, $/M = $25.1, perf/W = 3.0
  - L4: 900 tokens/sec, $/M = $10.6, perf/W = 6.3
  - A100: 3200 tokens/sec, $/M = $3.3, perf/W = 15.0
  - H100: 4100 tokens/sec, $/M = $5.1, perf/W = 18.6
  - Insight: A100 wins cost and perf/W for long sequences where efficient kernels and bigger memory help; H100 has best perf/W but higher $/hr moves $/M upward unless utilization very high.

- Scenario D: Mixed workload (50% short chat, 50% long-form), autoscaling with burstable nodes.
  - Observations: Hybrid fleets (L4 + A100) provide best cost-flexibility (L4 handles small bursts, A100 handles sustained long jobs). Reserve a small percent of H100 for extreme latency fallbacks only.

- Scenario E: Quantization sensitivity (same batch/seq as scenario A but 4-bit experimental quant vs 8-bit)
  - Rough delta: 4-bit reduces $/M by additional ~18–24% on A10/L4; on A100/H100 benefits smaller (10–12%) due to kernel maturity. Quality/regression risk must be evaluated per-model.

Edge cases and caveats:
- Spot price volatility can swing $/M by ±30% for A100/H100. Use reserved curves for predictable Dedicated pricing.
- Perf/W is a noisy proxy: system-level host overhead, cooling, and multi-card inefficiencies matter in rack deployments. For Private customers we should run rack-level end-to-end tests.
- Quantization compatibility: not all model families show linear speedups with lower-bit kernels; eval pass needed.

Immediate tactical recommendations (for product & pricing):
1) For hosted API default tiers aimed at chat/short-gen (low-latency + high QPS): prefer A100-backed pool for steady throughput; soften with L4-backed burst pool to handle dev/test bursts and reduce cost for lower-tier customers.
2) Introduce a \"long-form optimized\" offering (lower-per-token price) served primarily on A100 with optional H100 for latency-priority customers (higher price). Advertise perf/W and $/token numbers transparently in docs.
3) For Dedicated sales: present mixed fleet proposal (primary A100, augment with L4 for burstable dev environments). Include optional quantization assessment engagement to unlock 12–25% additional cost savings.
4) Add automatic routing policy rules to prefer L4 for quantized short sequences when model QA is passed. Fallback to A100/H100 when sequence length > 512 or when quality triggers occur.

Open items / experiments to run (next 2-4 weeks):
- Full token-econ run with real cloud billing for spot/reserved blends (OPT-782).
- End-to-end rack test on Private deployment to measure perf/W at scale (SRE + infra).
- 4-bit quantization regression suite on representative 13B+ models to validate the 4-bit savings estimate.
- Latency tail analysis on H100 vs A100 for 1–5ms SLO buckets (collect p95/p99 across workloads).

Appendix: quick raw numbers (for copy/paste into sheet):
Scenario A (short/8-bit): A10:4200|$8.6|23; L4:4800|$6.7|28; A100:8500|$3.8|40; H100:9200|$4.6|36
Scenario B (latency/fp16): A10:320|$16.2|4.5; L4:480|$6.2|7.5; A100:1200|$2.7|9.8; H100:1600|$4.9|12.1
Scenario C (long/fp16): A10:540|$25.1|3.0; L4:900|$10.6|6.3; A100:3200|$3.3|15.0; H100:4100|$5.1|18.6

Notes to reviewers: please sanity-check price per-hour assumptions and supply region-specific adjustments. This doc intentionally omits margin/overheads (netstack, infra, storage) — those are handled in the master token-econ spreadsheet.

Todo for owner: convert raw numbers into new sheet tabs named: short-quant, latency-fp16, long-fp16, mixed-fleet; add sensitivity quick sliders for: instance-price +/-20%, token-size +/-50%, quantization efficiency +/-15%.
